arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Waxman argued that due process requires counsel before incarceration in civil contempt cases.
Mr. Bibas argued that a per se right to counsel is not essential to prevent unfairness.
Ms. Kruger argued that due process requires a meaningful opportunity to be heard on ability to pay.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the procedural rights of a noncustodial parent in a civil contempt proceeding. The core issue is whether the threat of incarceration triggers a constitutional right to appointed counsel. The lower court denied the request for a lawyer. the side that brought the case argues this denial violated due process. the opposing side argues the hearing was fair without one.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the minimum procedural protections for parents facing jail time for unpaid support. It clarifies the balance between state enforcement powers and individual liberty interests. The outcome shapes how courts handle financial disputes involving potential incarceration.
